title: Emerging network model in a twisted monolayer-rhombohedral graphene
authors: Juyoung Song, Jeyong Park, Jinhong Park
abstract: We investigate the coexistence of localized states and propagating one-dimensional (1D) modes in graphene moiré systems. We first show within a minimal model that a spatially varying scalar potential can confine localized states, while sign changes of a staggered potential generate 1D modes along the resulting domain walls. These two types of states can coexist within the same finite energy window and form a hybrid network. We then demonstrate a microscopic realization of this mechanism in twisted monolayer-rhombohedral N-layer graphene. Band structures, energy contours, and Bloch wave functions obtained in a realistic parameter regime reveal the coexistence of localized nearly flat-band states and propagating quasi-1D modes. Our results establish twisted monolayer-rhombohedral graphene as a promising platform for realizing hybrid electronic networks with coexisting states of distinct effective dimensionalities.
summary: This work theoretically investigates the formation of hybrid electronic networks in twisted rhombohedral graphene by analyzing the coexistence of localized and propagating 1D electronic states. Using an effective Hamiltonian derived from moiré potentials, the authors demonstrate that this system naturally supports distinct types of electronic behavior across its lattice structure.
main_problem: The study investigates the coexistence of localized electronic states and propagating one-dimensional (1D) modes within moiré graphene systems.
main_result: The authors establish twisted monolayer–rhombohedral graphene as a promising platform for realizing hybrid electronic networks exhibiting coexisting states of distinct effective dimensionalities.
method: The analysis uses continuum models and perturbation theory to derive an effective low-energy Hamiltonian acting on the monolayer graphene, incorporating spatially varying potentials derived from moiré patterns.
model_or_system: The physical system is twisted monolayer–rhombohedral N-layer graphene. The model involves deriving an effective Moiré Hamiltonian by integrating out the gapped rhombohedral substrate layer, resulting in terms dependent on a scalar potential ($V_0$) and a staggered potential ($V_s$).
key_observables: Band structures (showing 1D bands and flat bands), constant-energy contours, real-space probability distributions of Bloch wave functions.
important_parameters: The relative twist angle ($	heta$), the energy regime within the gap ($U_{N+1} < E < U_2$), and characteristic length scales ($\xi$).
main_assumptions: Key approximations include using a minimal parametrization for potentials, neglecting lattice-relaxation-induced corrugation, and employing the local approximation in the effective Hamiltonian derivation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the moiré pattern, spatial profiles of $V_s(\mathbf{r})$ (showing sign changes) and $V_0(\mathbf{r})$ (showing minima), band structures showing both 1D and flat bands, and constant-energy contours confirming quasi-1D propagation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from a minimal toy model analysis demonstrating the coexistence of localized states (from $V_0$) and 1D modes (from sign changes in $V_s$), to a full microscopic realization using twisted multilayer graphene, where the effective Hamiltonian is derived via perturbation theory.
why_interesting: The emergence of distinct electronic dimensionalities (localized vs. quasi-1D) within a single moiré lattice structure provides a rich playground for studying correlated electron physics, potentially leading to novel topological or superconducting phases.
